item.title: Portable fan problems 手持小风扇引发的问题
item.description:
近年来，手持小风扇逐渐成为了炎炎夏日里的 “时尚单品”。不过，有研究指出，廉价、劣质的手持小风扇以及其它各类 “fast technology（快科技）” 产品往往容易被人们用后即弃。这不仅会增加电子垃圾的数量，还会给垃圾回收设施带来安全隐患，并可能导致重金属污染。本文简要介绍手持小风扇给人类社会和自然环境带来的问题。

词汇：electronic fans 电风扇

1  They could be the hottest accessory of an even hotter summer. As temperature records were smashed across Europe and other parts of the world, portable electric fans could be seen in the hands of millions of people. Estimates claim that up to 8 million of these devices were sold in the UK alone. The breeze that they provide will have been welcome to many, but could there be a downside to this popular product?

2  Concerns have been raised that these fans are just another example of fast technology. That is products that are sold cheaply and are likely to be disposed of quickly. Research from Material Focus, a British pro-recycling organisation, suggests that half of all the mini fans bought will end up unused or thrown away. This is unsurprising as they can be cheap to buy and almost impossible to repair. Fans contain a mix of different materials – plastic casing, copper wiring and a lithium-ion battery among other components. This means that a considerable amount of natural resource is used in their production, and that they can be complex to recycle and dispose of sustainably.

3  There are more immediate safety risks from portable fans. The London Fire Brigade has reported cases of cheaply-made portable fan batteries catching fire or exploding while being charged. Waste disposal companies in the UK have warned that the lithium-ion batteries used by these devices are often thrown away together with household waste, and that this can lead to fires which put staff and installations at risk. It's not just fire either. The Japanese Consumer Affairs Agency reports a train passenger's hair being sucked into someone else's fan on a train. In addition, once the air around you gets hot enough, fans can even make you warmer rather than colder.

4  As the world's climate continues to heat up, more and more of us may be tempted to reach for portable fans. But maybe we should take some time to reflect on the effect this might be having on our environment and climate.

测验与练习

一、将标题和段落配对。

Paragraph 1 _______
Paragraph 2 _______
Paragraph 3 _______
Paragraph 4 _______

a. Fast technology, hard to dispose of
b. Responsible choices
c. Greenhouse gases
d. A heatwave hit
e. Safety risks

二、根据文章内容选出正确的选项。

1. Summer temperatures have been high in Europe.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

2. What does 'fast technology' mean in this article?
a. technology with fast motors
b. cheap and disposable technology
c. technology that is fast to manufacture

3. What does 'this' refer to in the following sentence? This is unsurprising as they can be cheap to buy and almost impossible to repair.
a. portable mini fans
b. half of mini fans being unused or thrown away
c. research from Material Focus

4. Which part of portable mini fans is likely to catch fire?
a. the casing
b. the wiring
c. the battery

5. A fan will always cool you down.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

三、用下列单词完成对本文的总结。

Portable electric fans have become the latest must-have 1) _______. They're a cheap way to feel a 2) _______ on a hot summer day. However, concerns have been raised about how often they just end up 3) _______. Many of their 4) _______ are hard to dispose of in a sustainable way. There have also been cases where their batteries 5) _______.

breeze
components
wiring
waste
disposal
accessory
thrown away
catch fire

（答案见词汇表后）

词汇表

accessory 配饰
breeze 凉风
fast technology 快科技，更新换代快、价格低廉的科技产品
dispose of 丢弃
throw away 扔掉，丢掉
casing 外壳
copper 铜制的
wiring 线缆，线路
lithium-ion battery 锂离子电池
component 部件，组成部分
sustainably 以可持续的方式，可持续地
catch fire 起火，着火
waste disposal 废弃物处理，垃圾处理
household waste 生活垃圾
installation 设施，装置，设备

答案

一、将标题和段落配对。

Paragraph 1 d) A heatwave hit
Paragraph 2 a) Fast technology, hard to dispose of
Paragraph 3 e) Safety risks
Paragraph 4 b) Responsible choices 

二、根据文章内容选出正确的选项。

1. a. True. As temperature records were smashed across Europe and other parts of the world, portable electric fans could be seen in the hands of millions of people.

2. b. That is products that are sold cheaply and likely to be disposed of quickly.

3. b. The pronoun 'this' refers back to the fact that half of mini fans are left unused or thrown away, mentioned in the previous sentence.

4. c. The London Fire Brigade has reported cases of cheaply-made portable fan batteries catching fire or exploding while being charged

5. b. In addition, once the air around you gets hot enough, fans can even make you warmer rather than colder. 

三、用下列单词完成对本文的总结。 

Portable electric fans have become the latest must-have accessory. They're a cheap way to feel a breeze on a hot summer day.  However, concerns have been raised about how often they just end up thrown away. Many of their components are hard to dispose of in a sustainable way. There have also been cases where their batteries catch fire.

item.title: The peacock effect: Why overconfidence can be good for you 孔雀效应：为什么过度自信可能对你有好处
item.description:
大多数人都更容易高估自己的聪明才智与经验技巧。如果自身能力不足以匹配这种认知，往往会引发严重的后果。但对于某些人来说，过度自信是否也能带来一些好处呢？阅读本文，了解 “overconfidence（过度自信）” 背后的心理学原理，以及为何研究人员会将其与孔雀的华丽羽毛联系在一起。

词汇：confidence 自信

1 Do you know anyone who is more confident in their own abilities than their actual performance suggests they should be? Perhaps they think they are an incredible singer, but they're actually tone-deaf. Most people believe that they are more intelligent and skilful than the average person, according to a 2020 meta-analysis by Zell and colleagues. Obviously, this cannot be the case. Overconfidence has a cost – it can lead to things like poor financial decisions and dangerous driving. So why do we have such a tendency to overestimate our abilities?

2 Excessive self-belief requires self-deception – believing your own falsehoods. An evolutionary perspective argues that humans evolved self-deception so that we could deceive others more easily. The theory goes that if you believe your own lies about your abilities, you're less likely to display behaviours which will give it away, such as nervousness or hesitation. Deceiving others about your abilities may enable you to open doors, but it is when you have to prove yourself that overconfidence can lead to costly mistakes. For those who have a greater underlying ability, though, overconfidence can be highly beneficial.

3 This is what researchers are calling the 'peacock's tail for people'. Peacocks have long and brightly coloured feathers to attract females, but they are extremely burdensome. The feathers are heavy and highly visible to predators, so only the healthiest peacocks can afford to carry such elaborate plumage. In other words, their feathers are a reliable indicator of their suitability for potential mates. Authors of a 2026 study, published in the Psychological Review compare this phenomenon with human overconfidence. They argue that only the most capable people can keep a high self-belief without suffering severe consequences. In other words, overconfidence may actually be a useful signal of ability.

4 So, what lessons can be learnt from all this? If you have a high ability in a particular skill, make sure you have the confidence to match it. Ability can bring success, but remember, it is confidence which opens the doors in the first place.

测验与练习

一、将标题和段落配对。

Paragraph 1 _______
Paragraph 2 _______
Paragraph 3 _______
Paragraph 4 _______
Paragraph 5 _______

a. The advice
b. Confident humans are like healthy peacocks
c. Overconfidence is part of human evolution
d. Teenagers tend to have a lack of confidence
e. The costs of overconfidence

二、根据文章内容选出正确的选项。

1. Most people are overconfident.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

2. Overconfidence is always a good thing.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

3. When you believe your own lies about your abilities, you are more likely to…
a. deceive others effectively.
b. be nervous or hesitate.
c. make costly mistakes.

4. Authors of the 2026 study compare peacock feathers to…
a. human health.
b. human ability.
c. human overconfidence.

5. The article writer argues that overconfidence is…
a. mostly positive.
b. mostly negative.
c. neither positive nor negative.

三、用下列单词完成对本文的总结。

Humans have a 1) _______ to be overconfident, believing their 2) _______ is better than it actually is. Confidence may make it easier to 3) _______ people about your abilities, but once you've opened the doors, you then have to 4) _______, and if your abilities don't match up, negative consequences can follow. But success can come when high 5) _______ is balanced with a high level of ability.

self-belief
performance
phenomenon
deceive
tendency
burdensome
prove yourself

（答案见词汇表后）

词汇表

performance 表现
tone-deaf 五音不全的
tendency 倾向，趋势
overestimate 高估
self-belief 自信，自我信念
self-deception 自我欺骗
falsehood 谎言，虚假陈述
deceive 欺骗
give (something) away 泄漏，暴露（某事）
hesitation 犹豫
prove oneself 证明自己
underlying 潜在的，根本的，深层的
peacock 孔雀
burdensome 沉重的
elaborate 华丽繁复的
plumage 全身羽毛，羽衣
phenomenon 现象

答案

一、将标题和段落配对。

Paragraph 1 e) The costs of overconfidence
Paragraph 2 c) Overconfidence is part of human evolution
Paragraph 3 b) Confident humans are like healthy peacocks
Paragraph 4 a) The advice

二、根据文章内容选出正确的选项。

1. a. True. Most people believe that they are more intelligent and skilful than the average person, according to a 2020 meta-analysis by Zell and colleagues.

2. b. False. Overconfidence has a cost – it can lead to things like poor financial decisions and dangerous driving. 

3. a. An evolutionary perspective argues that humans evolved self-deception so that we could deceive others more easily.

4. c. Authors of a 2026 study, published in the Psychological Review compare this phenomenon [the display of peacock feathers] with human overconfidence.

5. a. While overconfidence can be costly, it is largely positive due to its ability to open doors for people and be a useful signal of ability for those observing. 

三、用下列单词完成对本文的总结。

Humans have a tendency to be overconfident, believing their performance is better than it actually is. Confidence may make it easier to deceive people about your abilities, but once you've opened the doors, you then have to prove yourself, and if your abilities don't match up, negative consequences can follow. But success can come when high self-belief is balanced with a high level of ability.

item.title: Why don't I like rollercoasters anymore? 为什么我不再喜欢坐过山车了?
item.description:
小时候，过山车带来的惊险和刺激总让人乐此不疲。但随着年龄增长，身体的变化和对风险认知的提高，可能会让乘坐过山车变得不再那么轻松愉快。为什么人们在童年时期往往更能享受坐过山车的乐趣呢？阅读本文，了解其背后的科学原理，以及如何在长大后依然享受过山车带来的刺激。

词汇：thrill-seeking 寻求刺激

1 Rollercoasters have been making stomachs flip for centuries. The earliest versions appeared in 17th-century Russia, where brave riders slid down giant ice-covered ramps. Modern steel rollercoasters transformed theme parks into thrill-seeking playgrounds. Today, they're bigger, faster and taller than ever. Millions of people queue for hours just to experience a few minutes of screaming, laughing and that heart-racing drop. But if you're anything like me, there comes a point when those rides stop feeling exciting and start feeling... slightly regrettable.

2 As children, rollercoasters seem almost impossible to resist. Part of the appeal is that contrasting mix of fear and excitement. According to BBC Science Focus, rollercoasters trigger the body's fight-or-flight response, releasing adrenaline, dopamine and endorphins that make the experience feel exciting and rewarding. Our brains quickly learn to associate that rush with fun, which is why so many children can't wait to jump back in the queue. The sense of achievement doesn't hurt either – finally being tall enough to ride the biggest coaster feels like a rite of passage, making us feel braver and probably way cooler at the time.

3 So why does that love affair often fade with age? Unfortunately, our bodies change. WanderWisdom explains that changes in the inner ear as we get older can make us more sensitive to motion, meaning rollercoasters that once felt thrilling may now leave us feeling dizzy or nauseous. Motion sickness happens when the brain receives conflicting signals from the eyes and inner ear, leading to dizziness, nausea and that feeling of churning in your tummy. Add stiffer joints, sore necks and a stronger awareness of risk, and it's hardly surprising that the rides we once begged to go on can suddenly feel more exhausting than exhilarating.

4 The good news is that you don't have to completely give up coasters. Dramamine recommends staying hydrated, avoiding heavy meals before riding and looking towards the horizon instead of down at the tracks. Choosing a seat towards the middle can also make the ride feel less intense. These simple changes may reduce motion sickness and help you to rediscover the fun of laughing and screaming along the way without feeling the need to hurl or pass out as often!

测验与练习

一、为本文选择总结句。

a. Everyone loves rollercoasters when they're a kid.
b. It's impossible for you to get over your dislike of rollercoasters.
c. There are some things you can do to help make rollercoasters feel enjoyable.

二、 根据文章内容选出正确的选项。

1. The first rollercoasters were built from steel.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

2. According to the text, why do many children enjoy rollercoasters so much?
a. Their brains associate the rush of adrenaline with fun.
b. They are less likely to feel motion sickness than adults.
c. They enjoy waiting in long queues.

3. As people get older, changes to the inner ear can make rollercoasters feel more uncomfortable.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

4. Which of the following is NOT suggested as a way to reduce motion sickness?
a. Close your eyes throughout the ride.
b. Sit towards the middle of the ride.
c. Stay hydrated.

5. The writer says that adults should stop riding rollercoasters completely.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

三、用下列单词完成对本文的总结。

Have you ever felt like you might 1) _______ while riding a rollercoaster as an adult? Though you might experience a slight 2) _______, you're more likely as an adult to find rollercoasters 3) _______. This could be because of how 4) _______ our bodies become as we age, or that the changes in our ears make us feel 5) _______ from the motion of the ride.

beg
contrasting
dizzy
pass out
regrttable
rush
stiff

（答案见词汇表后）

词汇表

flip 翻腾
slide 滑行
thrill-seeking 追求刺激的
queue 排队
regrettable 令人后悔的
resist 抵挡，抗拒
contrasting 截然不同的，形成对比的
trigger 引发，触发
endorphin 内啡肽
rush 强烈的刺激感，兴奋感
rite of passage 成长的必经阶段
dizzy 头晕目眩的
conflicting 相互矛盾的
churning （胃里）翻腾的，反胃的
stiffer 更僵硬的
beg 恳求
exhilarating 令人兴奋的，令人振奋的
horizon 地平线
intense 剧烈的，强烈的
rediscover 重新找回，重新发现
hurl 呕吐
pass out 失去知觉，昏倒 

答案

一、 为本文选择总结句。

c. There are some things you can do to help make rollercoasters feel enjoyable

二、根据文章内容选出正确的选项。

1. b. False. The earliest versions appeared in 17th-century Russia, where brave riders slid down giant ice-covered ramps.

2. a. Our brains quickly learn to associate that rush with fun, which is why so many children can't wait to jump straight back in the queue.

3. a. True. Changes to the inner ear as we get older can make us more sensitive to motion, meaning rollercoasters that once felt thrilling may now leave us feeling dizzy or nauseous

4. a. The text recommends staying hydrated, avoiding heavy meals before riding and looking towards the horizon instead of down at the tracks. Choosing a seat towards the middle can also make the ride feel less intense. It does not recommend closing your eyes.

5. b. False. The good news is that you don't have to completely give up coasters.

三、用下列单词完成对本文的总结。

Have you ever felt like you might pass out while riding a roller coaster as an adult? Though you might experience a slight rush, you’re more likely as an adult to find rollercoasters regrettable. This could be because of how stiff our bodies become as we age, or that the changes in our ears make us feel dizzy from the motion of the ride.

item.title: How seasons affect our moods 四季如何影响我们的情绪
item.description:
“春困秋乏夏打盹”，这句汉语俗语的背后是季节与人类情绪状态之间复杂的联系。从阳光明媚的春天到阴郁的冬日，我们的情绪和激素水平不断波动，塑造着我们对季节的独特印象。此外，每个人对四季的身体反应也不大相同。阅读本文，了解四季的更替究竟在如何调节我们的身体和情绪。

词汇：seasons 四季

1 We have four seasons in the UK. I like to think that spring gets its name from the flowers springing up to bloom. Next is my personal favourite – summer. I love the long, balmy evenings. Autumn, as some call fall, comes after. It's characterised by the orange and red leaves. Winter rolls around, and most of the vegetation is either decomposing or already dead, and the days are short and gloomy.

2 It's no wonder that, according to the Royal College of Psychiatrists, about three in every hundred people in the UK experience seasonal affective disorder, otherwise known as SAD. However, researchers at the Royal College of Psychiatrists have discovered that all seasons have an impact on our psychological functioning. It's also been found that hormones play an important role in seasonal mood changes as they fluctuate throughout the year.

3 An article published on Springer Nature Link observes positive emotional and physical changes to volunteers who were exposed to UVA from the Sun. Serotonin, known as 'the happy hormone', and dopamine, which is linked to motivation and pleasure, increases in months where there is a boost of sunlight. Similarly, lovers of spring recalibrate their energy and mood. After the cold, dark seasons of autumn and winter, it can feel like a biological reset.

4 Speaking of cold and dark, this is when those with naturally higher serotonin levels feel their mood regulating. They no longer feel overwhelmed by the high-level serotonin seasons of spring and summer. Reduced sunlight triggers higher melatonin, the sleepy hormone. There is the notion of preparing to slow down and get cosy, like that of animals in hibernation. It also rains more in autumn and winter. The Mind Company says that rain sounds reduce cortisol, the stress hormone, and helps you relax, focus and even sleep better.

5 We might like one season more than others. Our experience of seasons differs depending on location and environment. But one thing is for sure – our feelings change from season to season, and recognising these changes can help us act in ways that are in-line with our mental, emotional and physical capabilities.

测验与练习

一、为本文选择总结句。

a. How we feel doesn't change season to season.
b. How we feel may change depending on the season.
c. How we feel will determine the weather.

二、根据文章内容选出正确的选项。

1. Which season in the UK sees leaves on the trees change from green to orange?
a. autumn
b. winter
c. spring

2. Our hormones change throughout the year.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

3. Sunny weather may increase _______ levels.
a. cortisol
b. dopamine
c. melatonin

4. People may prefer autumn and winter because…
a. there is less rainfall than spring and summer.
b. there is more sunlight than in spring and summer.
c. they feel overwhelmed by spring and summer.

5. The writer understands that people experience seasons differently.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

三、用下列单词完成对本文的总结。

When we welcome a new season, our hormones 1) _______. This 2) _______ some changes in how we feel and behave. Some of us feel like we need a 3) _______ in sunlight to be happy. Others find peace in 4) _______ nights spent inside by a fireplace. Regardless of which season you prefer, it’s good to check in with yourself. This will help 5) _______ your emotions and direct your actions towards positivity.

balmy
boost
cosy
fluctuate
recalibrates
regulate
triggers

（答案见词汇表后）

词汇表

spring up 冒出来
bloom 绽放
balmy 温暖舒适的
roll around 再次到来
decompose 腐烂，分解
gloomy 阴郁的
disorder 疾病，紊乱
functioning 功能，运作
fluctuate 波动，起伏不定
UVA 长波紫外线
boost 增多，增强
recalibrate 重新调整
reset 重置
regulate 调节，稳定
overwhelm 使...不知所措，令...难以承受
trigger 导致，引起
notion 概念
cosy 舒适的，惬意的
hibernation 冬眠
in-line with 与…相似，与…处于同等水平

答案

一、为本文选择总结句。

b. How we feel may change depending on the season.

二、根据文章内容选出正确的选项。

1. a. Autumn, as some call fall, comes after. It's characterised by the orange and red leaves.

2. a. True. It's also been found that hormones play an important role in seasonal mood changes as they fluctuate throughout the year.

3. b. Serotonin, known as the happy hormone, and dopamine, which is linked to motivation and pleasure, increases in months where there is a boost of sunlight.

4. c. Speaking of cold and dark, this is when those with naturally higher serotonin levels feel their mood regulating. They no longer feel overwhelmed by the high-level serotonin seasons of spring and summer.

5. a. True. We might like one season more than others. Our experience of seasons differs depending on location and environment.

三、用下列单词完成对本文的总结。

When we welcome a new season, our hormones fluctuate. This triggers some changes in how we feel and behave. Some of us feel like we need a boost in sunlight to be happy. Others find peace in cosy nights spent inside by a fireplace. Regardless of which season you prefer, it’s good to check in with yourself. This will help regulate your emotions and direct your actions more positively.

item.title: Which English accent is the oldest? 哪一种英语口音历史最悠久？
item.description:
据估计，英国拥有大约 40 到 60 种地方英语口音。许多人认为，听上去更优雅、更具格调的南方口音才是英国上流社会人士或历史剧中人物所说的英语。不过，只要对英国的语言发展历史稍加了解，就会发现南方口音很可能并非英国最古老的口音。英语的演变历程比大多数人想象的更加复杂和曲折。阅读本文，了解英语发展史上的几个重要阶段，以及最古老的英语口音最有可能来自哪个地区。

词汇：language 语言

1 Would you like to speak with a British accent? What if I told you that there is no singular 'British' accent? In fact, linguists estimate that there are 40-60 regional accents across the UK, some of which exist very close together geographically. For instance, you can listen to Manchester's 'Mancunian' accent and then Liverpool's distinct 'Scouse' accent after just a 50-minute car or train ride. Some southern English accents, such as 'Received Pronunciation', are associated with social prestige, but can the south claim to have the oldest English accent? Or does another UK region take the title? The story is messier than you might expect.

2 The first version of English, Old English, originated in the 5th and 6th centuries when tribes from northern Germany arrived in east England, a region now called 'East Anglia'. Their Germanic languages mixed with existing Latin and Celtic languages and became Old English. "It makes sense to think of East Anglia as being the source of the earliest variety of English as we know it," says Kerri-Ann Butcher, a lecturer in English Language at the University of Leeds. Over the next few centuries, English absorbed many other languages arriving from places like the Netherlands and Scandinavia. The associated linguistic changes did not happen in an orderly way across the country.

3 With all these different influences, the English language became messy and inconsistent. But in 1476, some spelling norms became standardised with the arrival of the printing press. Nowadays, the words 'blood', 'food' and 'good', which all contain two letter Os, sound different, but back then, they might have rhymed. Between the 12th and 18th centuries, something known as the Great Vowel Shift happened, where some vowel sounds across the country changed. For example, the vowel sound in 'foot' and 'strut' used to be pronounced the same, but then people in the south began pronouncing 'strut' differently. Danielle Turton, sociolinguist at Lancaster University, says the northern pronunciation is absolutely the original one. "It was the south that branched off and created this new vowel."
 
4 So, there you have it. While East Anglia may have been the home of the earliest English sounds, it did not stick to the original pronunciations like accents in northern England did. And while many think Received Pronunciation is an older-sounding English, in fact, it didn't exist until the 18th century. The north of England wins!

测验与练习

一、将标题和段落配对。

Paragraph 1 _______
Paragraph 2 _______
Paragraph 3 _______
Paragraph 4 _______
Paragraph 5 _______

a. The north-south divide
b. A French invasion
c. Britain's linguistic variation
d. American English
e. The origins of the English language
f. The oldest English accent

二、根据文章内容选出正确的选项。

1. Which accent is typically associated with the English city of Liverpool?
a. Mancunian
b. Scouse
c. Received Pronunciation

2. Old English is a mix of Germanic, Latin and Celtic languages.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

item.title: The art of farts 关于 “肠道排气” 的科学
item.description:
它常常让人感到尴尬、难以启齿，甚至在公共场合极力避免发生，但本文将试着从一个全新的角度探讨 “fart（屁）” 这一自然的生理现象。其实，对大多数哺乳动物来说，放屁是消化系统的正常运作的表现之一。而对部分动物来说，比如蛇类和昆虫，放屁甚至是求生、防御或沟通的手段。阅读短文，了解屁背后的科学解释。

词汇：biology 生物学

1  It's a topic people usually avoid, yet it's a universal human experience. Flatulence, affectionately known as farting, is simply the releasing of gas from the backside. The word itself traces back to the Latin 'flatus', which literally means 'a blowing' or 'wind.' While it is often the butt of the joke, we do it for very practical reasons, which boil down to digestion. Most mammals have a complex, symbiotic relationship with their gut microbes which break down food. Digestion requires a lengthy process of fermentation, and flatulence is simply the inevitable byproduct of these hard-working bacteria. Passing gas is a sign of a highly functioning digestive system.

2  But we humans aren't the only mammals that like to let one off. In 2017, National Geographic and the BBC reported the results of an online survey. It revealed some incredibly unlikely farters, like zebras, which have been documented farting withevery single step whilst running away from predators. On a bigger scale, cow flatulence and burps are packed with methane, a potent greenhouse gas that is actively driving global climate change. And, if you've ever had a domesticated pet, you might've even blamed your own farts on them! I know I have.

3  There are other fascinating examples of farting from the animal kingdom. The Sonoran coral snake expels air forcefully to startle predators when it's in danger. In an article published on The Conversation, it's mentioned that herring, a type of fish, will release gas as a way to communicate with each other that predators are nearby. It was also written in IFLScience that the beaded lacewing, a type of larva, can take down six termites with one fart!

4  So it seems that some animals pass gas as an evolutionary survival tactic. Those not so 'silent but deadly' farts can ward off predators as well as let others know that there's potential danger. While farts for us are mainly the result of digestion, perhaps, like the Sonoran snake, herring and beaded lacewing, we could embrace the breeze and utilise them against our enemies? Hahaha, just joking!

测验与练习

b. Farting is natural – a lot of animals fart.
c. Most mammal fart when they’re in danger.

b. helps slow down climate change.
c. makes a cow's gut healthier.

4. The gas released by herring contains toxic chemicals.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

5. The beaded lacewing larva can kill up to six termites at a time with a single fart.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

三、用下列单词完成对本文的总结。 

For most animals, farts are a natural 1) _______ of 2) _______ in the digestive system. But for some animals, they are used as a 3) _______ when they feel they’re in danger. They 4) _______ either to communicate with others about predators, or to 5) _______ predators, giving them a chance to escape!

startle

tactic

（答案见词汇表后）

答案

2. c. The Sonoran coral snake expels air forcefully to startle predators when it's in danger.

3. a. On a bigger scale, cow flatulence and burps are packed with methane, a potent greenhouse gas that is actively driving global climate change.

4. c. Not given. While the text confirms that herring use flatulence to communicate about nearby predators, it does not mention what kind of chemicals that the gas contains.

5. a. True. ...beaded lacwing, a type of larva, can take down six termites with one fart!

For most animals, farts are a natural byproduct of fermentation in the digestive system. But for some animals, they are used as a tactic when they feel they're in danger. They let one off either to communicate with others about predators, or to startle predators, giving them a chance to escape!

item.title: Gen Z's love of the past 热衷怀旧的 “Z 世代”
item.description:
越来越多的年轻人开始回首过去，从复古物件和旧日潮流中寻找慰藉和安全感。比如，他们重新迷上了有线耳机、唱片和笨重的数码相机等 “老式” 科技产品。本文将探讨一个有趣的问题：人们真的会怀念一个自己从未经历过的时代吗？

词汇：culture and nostalgia 文化和怀旧

1  Today's youth are reinventing what it means to be cool. A surprising number of Gen Zers are actively looking to the past. They are choosing to romanticise old-school tech relics like CDs, wired headphones, and weighty digital cameras. This love for all things vintage extends into their wardrobes with a massive resurgence of Y2K (year 2000) fashion. Friday nights are increasingly filled with board games and classic card games. So why exactly is the most digitally advanced generation trying so hard to rewind?

2  The answer lies in a desire to slow down and find comfort. Growing up as digital natives has its perks, but Profectus Magazine reveals that around 80% of Gen Z adults worry their generation is far too dependent on technology, while three-quarters feel social media is affecting their mental health. Swapping music streaming for physical CDs or endless social media scrolling for a tactile board game allows them to unplug and step away from the digital noise. 

3  This analogue revival could actually be good for everyone. Research by psychologist Dr. Clay Routledge shows that engaging with nostalgic media and traditions can dramatically boost positive moods, reduce anxiety and help people cope with daily stress. It suggests that nostalgia can act as a stabilising, hopeful force, helping a young generation build social confidence. 

4  Yet, all of this begs a fascinating question – can a generation truly yearn for a life they never actually lived? Studies published in Profectus Magazine show that nearly 70% of Gen Z adults experience a unique kind of historical nostalgia for eras that predated their own birth. GWI, a global market research company, reports that young people are looking back at the past through rose-tinted glasses, viewing it as a time of genuine human interaction.

5  Though there have been mixed reactions from millennials, ultimately, Gen Z's obsession with the past suggests that no matter how advanced our gadgets get, human beings may always desire a simpler way of living. For a generation that grew up entirely online, going vintage isn't just a fashion statement, it's a total vibe.

测验与练习

item.title: How to cope with disappointment 如何应对失望情绪
item.description:
对未能实现的目标和计划感到 “disappointment（失望）” 是人之常情。不过，如果让失望长期主导我们的心态，就难免得不偿失。缓解失望的关键在于缩小期待与现实之间的落差；有时，我们还可以将失望转化为前进的动力，从而发现更多可能性。阅读本文，了解失望情绪从何而来，以及我们可以如何从容应对它。

词汇：disappointment 失望

1  We've all been there. Ending up with a worse exam result than you had hoped for or expected, a friend cancelling a plan you were really looking forward to, or your favourite sports team losing a game. Disappointment is an unhappy feeling when there is a gap between your expectations and reality, when something you desired failed to materialise. It's a normal and natural reaction, but what to do? Is it best to forget about it and move on, or allow yourself to feel the feels?

2  We often can't control what happens in life, but we can control how we respond when things don't go our way. Dr Radha Modgil, a UK family doctor and campaigner for wellbeing, says that we should take time to process the disappointment. "We can often feel the need to move on straight away or ignore our feelings, but if we take time to process them and talk them through, we can move forward in a healthier way," she says. Next, she advises us to see the opportunities. Things may not have worked out this time, but when one door closes, a different, more exciting door may have opened, in a way that may one day make you grateful for the initial disappointment. 

3  The wider the gap between expectations and reality, the greater the disappointment. Make sure your goals are realistic, not idealistic, says Dr Annette Clancy, an organisational consultant who researches emotions in the workplace. Think about what a realistic result would be, rather than the perfect one. When waiting for something significant like a job offer or test result, her advice is to not get ahead of yourself. When we anticipate a positive result, we often start imagining a future that doesn't yet exist, and if that future doesn't materialise, we then have to grieve its loss, which can be upsetting. 

4  Try not to take it personally. Disappointment might make you think, "I'm not good enough," and lead you to blame yourself, affecting your self-esteem. It may cause you to blame others, making you angry that they did not recognise your value. Dr Annette Clancy says both reactions miss the point. Instead, see disappointment as a signal that our expectations and reality are not aligned. Understanding this, she says, can be an important way to develop resilience.

a. True
b. False
c. Not given

Instead, 2) _______ with someone you trust. 3) _______ allows you to process what happened and move on from the disappointment in a healthier way. In the future, make sure that your expectations and reality are roughly 4) _______. That way, if your desires don't 5) _______, the disappointment won't feel so damaging.

3. a. True. Make sure your goals are realistic, not idealistic, says Dr Annette Clancy, an organisational consultant who researches emotions in the workplace.

4. b. When we anticipate a positive result, we often start imagining a future that doesn't yet exist, and if that future doesn't materialise, we then have to grieve its loss, which can be upsetting.

5. c. Not given. The article recommends avoiding unachievable goals but doesn't mention avoiding ambitious goals.

三、用下列单词完成对本文的总结。

Feeling the feels allows you to process what happened and move on from the disappointment in a healthier way. In the future, make sure that your expectations and reality are roughly aligned. That way, if your desires don't materialise, the disappointment won't feel so damaging.

item.title: Birdwatching boom 观鸟热潮
item.description:
长期以来，“birdwatching（观鸟）” 都被许多人视作老一辈的爱好。随着科技的发展，年轻一代观鸟爱好者拥有了越来越丰富的装备，甚至还能借助根据鸟鸣识别鸟类品种的应用程序来观鸟。这些工具鼓励观鸟爱好者记录自己发现的鸟类，并与他人比较观测到的品种和数量。如今，这项古老的爱好再次焕发出了新的活力。阅读本文，了解观鸟如何成为英国年轻人中的新潮流。

词汇：nature 自然

1 Many young Brits are buying binoculars in hopes of encountering one of nature's most physically and audibly beautiful creatures - birds. You might think of birdwatching as an old-fashioned pastime most often enjoyed by the generations before you, but surveys conducted by the RSPB show a 47% increase in participation overall, with an even higher 1,088% surge by Gen Zers. So why do so many young people want to flock to the park to watch birds?

2 A group leader at RSPB Bristol highlighted how many students have joined his outings. He mentioned that some who join have 'never been out in their local nature spaces' and 'want to explore'. He added that the diversity of species you can find is impressive 'considering it's so urban' around the city. There is also the rise of a desire to disconnect from technology and go outside, or as Gen Z would call it touch grass, to help with mental health. Research from the University of Surrey has looked at how bird sounds restore attention and even alleviate stress.

3 Ironically, when interviewed by BBC Bristol, individuals mentioned how phones and social media have actually helped encourage the hype of this hobby. There are now a variety of apps in which you can record a birdsong and have it instantly identified. People also use social media to share knowledge and location for birds. A phenomenon known as 'bioblitzing', a combination of bio and blitzing, has emerged. This is when a walker documents as many birds and other species of animals as they can within a limited amount of time. It has been said to create a safe space in which birdwatchers can get into friendly competitions over who can spot the most! Furthermore, a buzz around the birdwatching hashtag has cultivated humour around turning 30 and entering your 'birdwatching era'.

4 Whether it's the chance to reconnect with nature, improve mental wellbeing, or join a growing online community, birdwatching is no longer seen as a hobby reserved for older generations. Young people are embracing it in record numbers, using both technology and the outdoors to discover the wildlife on their doorstep. From identifying birdsongs with apps to competing in bioblitzing challenges, a modern twist has transformed the pastime into something fresh and accessible. It seems that for Gen Z and young millennials alike, birdwatching has become a hoot.

item.title: How high temperatures affect sleep 高温对睡眠的影响
item.description:
为什么天气一热，我们就更难入睡？真相隐藏在人体的散热机制当中。当气温和湿度上升时，血管舒张、出汗等体温调节机制的效率会大打折扣。专家建议，在高温天气下，适当使用空调并保持良好的通风对营造舒适的睡眠环境尤为重要；选择更轻薄透气的床上用品和睡衣也有助于改善入睡时的体感温度。你是否也在为炎炎夏日里的睡眠问题而烦恼？阅读本文，了解应对高温的实用助眠小技巧。

词汇：hot weather and sleep 高温天气和睡眠

1  Around the world, summers are getting hotter. Day and night temperatures are increasing. What impact could that be having on how we sleep?

2  Temperature and sleep are closely linked. Typically, our bodies cool themselves down before we sleep. One of the main ways that we do this is by widening blood vessels near the skin to allow heat to dissipate. In hot weather, this process becomes less effective as it is more difficult for heat to be transferred. One of the body's mechanisms to speed up this process is by allowing sweat to evaporate. However, in humid conditions it's harder for evaporation to take place. If the body is unable to cool down, then it's more difficult for people to fall asleep and more likely that sleep patterns can be disrupted.

3  This means that it's important for us to try to manage the temperature of the environment that we sleep in. While it can be costly, air conditioning is a useful tool to keep our sleeping environment cool. Managing ventilation is also important. During the hottest hours of the day keeping windows and curtains closed can stop hot air and heat from sunlight entering our homes. At night, once the temperature has dropped, opening windows can allow cool air to come in and reduce the temperature in our homes. Fans can help to speed up cooling, as long as air temperatures are low enough. They become less effective in hotter conditions.

4  It's not just rooms that we can cool down. Using breathable bedding and sleepwear makes it easier for our bodies to regulate temperature. While it may seem counter-intuitive, it can be beneficial to have a warm bath or shower before sleep. Warm water can cause more blood to flow to our skin. Once you get out of the bath or shower, this means that you cool down more quickly. Another tip suggested by sleep experts Kevin Morgan and Lisa Artis is to cool your socks in the fridge and then put them on before going to sleep. They also say that it's important to try to keep to your usual sleep routine to avoid disruption to your sleep habits.

We can manage the temperature in our sleeping environment by using air conditioning or ensuring that there is sufficient 3) _______. Using 4) _______ fabrics for our 5) _______ can also help us to get a good night's sleep.

答案

Paragraph 2 a) Our body's natural cooling
Paragraph 3 d) Keeping bedrooms cool
Paragraph 4 c) Keeping yourself cool

二、根据文章内容选出正确的选项。

2. b. The pronoun 'this' refers to cooling our body down, mentioned in the previous sentence

3. c. One of the body's mechanisms to speed up this process is sweating. However, in humid conditions it is harder for evaporation to take place.

4. c. While it can be costly, air conditioning is a useful tool to keep our sleeping environment cool.

5. a. While it may seem counter-intuitive, it can be beneficial to have a warm bath or shower before sleep.

三、用方框中的单词完成对本文的总结。

Usually, before we sleep our bodies allow heat to dissipate to cool us down. In hot humid weather this mechanism is less effective making it harder for us to sleep. We can manage the temperature in our sleeping environment by using air conditioning or ensuring that there is sufficient ventilation. Using breathable fabrics for our bedding can also help us to get a good night's sleep.

item.title: Heat, humidity and the World Cup 世界杯面临高温高湿考验
item.description:
在今年的世界杯开赛前，天气预报就显示，举办赛事的多个城市将迎来温度和湿度 “双高” 的天气。对于运动员来说，这样的天气条件会带来哪些挑战？赛事主办方又采取了哪些措施来保障比赛安全、顺利进行？阅读本文，了解极端天气如何影响这项备受全球关注的体育赛事。

词汇：football and heat 足球和高温天气

1 Fans have been gathering across the US, Canada and Mexico, as well as the world's TV screens, to watch the 2026 men's football World Cup kick off. However, experts have been increasingly worried about the effect of summer heat and humidity on the competing players. High levels of both have been predicted for a number of the tournament venues.

2 Previous competitions held in similar conditions have caused difficulties for players and officials. Assistant referee Humberto Panjoj collapsed during a Copa America game in Kansas City in 2024. In a game in Miami in the same competition, Uruguayan defender Ronald Araujo was substituted, complaining of dehydration and dizziness. Players also complained about conditions at the 2025 Club World Cup in the US. Both these competitions were played in cities that feature in the 2026 World Cup. Sports Medicine Australia warns of the dangers of heat exhaustion, heat stroke and dehydration from exercising in hot and humid conditions.

3 Experts suggest that the key measure to assess risk from heat and humidity is the wet bulb globe temperature. When we sweat, it usually evaporates, cooling us down. Humid conditions make this process less effective. Wet bulb globe temperature is the minimum temperature achieved after water has evaporated. Many experts suggest that heat can be a problem for athletes if the wet bulb globe temperature is above 28C.

4 14 out of 16 of the World Cup venues have been forecast to have wet bulb globe temperatures above this level during normal summer afternoons. For this reason, many games have been moved to evening kick offs, and cooling breaks have been scheduled. Additionally, some stadiums have roofs and air-conditioning. However, concerns remain around evening games in Miami and Kansas City, which had been predicted to be hot and humid, and the final in New Jersey, which was scheduled for 3pm. Estimates are based on a normal summer. However, the situation would be considerably worse should there be a heatwave.
